selection: On/off control reusing IsolatedWorktreeCheck and ISOLATED_WORKTREE_LABEL, with the off state left silent.
rationale: Review Mode is Auto with review_gates empty, so the interface pick is the LLM's to make and is never parked on the card. The evidence chose it over the runner-up on a structural rather than a stylistic ground: a silent off state makes the unearned-promise failure impossible rather than merely worded away. opt-2 (radio-card) can only promise by explanation, and explanation is exactly what produced 'Project checkout' in the first place - lib/tracks.mjs:96 stores 'managed' for any project-default, so the label and the stored fact would disagree. opt-3 also inherits min-h-11 and cursor-pointer by construction (isolated-worktree-check.tsx:19-21), satisfying a house rule AGENTS.md itself admits is 'stated, not tested', and it inherits a running test pin (tests/card-start.test.mjs:150) plus an existing consumer.

rejected.why: Carries the same inexpressible-promise problem as opt-3 in weaker form: the off state must be explained, and a card that lands where BB's own default put it is not a defect to be warned about. Keeps a better unrecognised-value state (a third visible 'neither selected'), which is the one criterion on which it beats opt-3 - accepted as the cost of the pick, not overlooked.
rejected.secondary: Would fork the isolated-worktree vocabulary away from the module that declares itself its single source.

rejected.why: ChoiceCards house style is a legitimate and now-verified accessible shape, but it is still a two-option control and therefore still needs an off-state sentence. It refutes the spec's false uniqueness premise without solving the problem that premise was attached to.

The decision-maker's literal first reaction. Not unbuildable - storage, the RPC enum and the form union all carry it - but invalid as a reader-facing promise, because a card carrying a 'Project checkout' preset is stored with a different word than the control promised. This is the exact failure the request exists to fix. Recorded rather than dropped: it is the request's origin.

acceptedCosts: The control is a bare checkbox, not a grouped fieldset: the off state carries no sentence, and the AC 9 unrecognised-value case lives in help text alone. A fieldset could show 'neither option selected' as a third visual state - this is the one criterion where a grouped control is strictly better.
A visible reference cycle: isolated-worktree-check.tsx's help text points at Agent Presets, which would then render its own words.

supersedesClause.was: copying components/creation/strategy-picker.tsx:64-104, the only in-repo radio shape yielding WCAG 2.2 focus appearance today
supersedesClause.now: reuse of the concept's declared single source (isolated-worktree-check.tsx / ISOLATED_WORKTREE_LABEL); the uniqueness claim was false and is withdrawn, corrected at source in plans/spec-product.md with all three in-repo shapes tabulated

carriedToGate: The decision-maker has not been shown that their own phrase 'project checkout' is the unearned promise. It is recorded in state.md and the spec, never confirmed back to them - so this pick must land as an explained re-labelling, not a silent one.
No first-reader pass distinguishes a checkbox with a silent off state from 'not set up yet'. The pick rests on structure, not on observed comprehension.
Whether the visible reference cycle is acceptable to the author of the isolated-worktree module is unasked; the module's comment shows the words are deliberately centralised.
coordinatorVerification: Every claim the contrast relied on was re-read directly in the checkout before this receipt was written: creation-settings.tsx:91 (ChoiceCards carries the identical focus treatment plus min-h-11 and cursor-pointer), isolated-worktree-check.tsx:8-14 and :19-21 (declared single source; min-h-11 and cursor-pointer), lib/tracks.mjs:94-100 ('managed' for any project-default), preset-assign-options.tsx:76-88 (no focus rule - the one reuse claim that IS correct).
